title: Skill Discovery and Progressive Disclosure
service: SkillCat: the skill layer of an agent host, with shallow discovery over ranked scopes, collision policy with shadowed candidates kept in diagnostics, package containment for resource reads, the model-facing catalog, a JSON snapshot of discovery invalidated by SKILL.md digests, the 2 percent / 8,000-character catalog budget, logfmt disclosure events and the reference graph of a package

parts.lesson_anchor: Why discovery is shallow; Scope is runtime policy (explicit integer rank, never precedence from directory names); Collisions need identity beyond name (shadowed candidates kept in diagnostics); Resource paths are a trust boundary (resolve root and candidate, symlinks checked on the resolved target); code/main.py discover_scope, resolve_collisions, validate_reference and the build_catalog while loop
planted_bugs: package_dirs uses root.rglob('SKILL.md'), so skill-author/examples/release-readiness becomes a second workspace package; the error surfaces in resolve_collisions as an equal-rank CollisionError, reached through SkillHost.catalog and build_catalog, while the cause sits on the discovery call chain

resolve_collisions sorts each name's candidates by (path, rank), so the alphabetically first directory wins: the builtin scope under agent-runtime/ beats the workspace under repo/; the tie check uses min(rank), so equal-rank duplicates are still caught
validate_reference checks containment on the unresolved path, which is always inside the root, so references/team-notes.md -> <tmp>/private/sign-off.md is accepted
build_catalog pops one entry at a time and serializes the whole catalog again after each pop (the lesson's while loop), O(n^2) in the number of entries
parts.timing_assert: build_catalog on 1,800 candidates with max_catalog_chars 6,000 under 0.15 s, timed after gc.collect() so the collection of the freshly built candidates is not counted. In pytest at load 4 to 10: quadratic starter 1.78-2.77 s over 16 runs (at least 11.9x the limit); fixed reference 3.8-5.3 ms over 20 runs (at least 28x under it). Standalone, the fixed version takes 1.5-5.0 ms over 120 runs; binary-search and precomputed-size fixes take 4-8 ms
parts.overfix_guard: two rank-3 plugins with pdf-tools still raise CollisionError (catches deleting the tie check to silence the first error); tests/fixtures/minimal-skill (catches skipping examples/ only); a three-way collision with shadowed candidates best rank first; references/latest.md -> python-release.md must resolve (catches refusing every symlink); references/vendor is a symlinked directory leaving the package (catches checking only the last component); the package is reached through a symlinked root (catches resolving the target but not the root); a missing reference raises ReferencePathError, not FileNotFoundError (catches strict resolve); catalog_chars equals len(model_json(entries)), entries are a prefix, omitted keeps priority order, an exact fit is kept and budget-cut names come before max_entries-cut names (catches running totals without commas or with default separators, skip-and-continue, reversed omitted, >=, appended omitted)

parts.lesson_anchor: Discovery is a compiler pipeline (structured data and structured failures: candidates, rejections and reasons); Use It 10 (rebuild the catalog when installations or policies change); Collisions need identity beyond name
parts.exactness: after a reopen, cache.discover(scope) equals discover_scope(scope) exactly: SkillCandidate with a Path source, metadata as a tuple of (key, value) tuples and a literal-block description with a newline, Rejection with its reason, under a root path with spaces and non-ASCII names; parsed lists exactly the packages inspected

snapshot kept in memory only
the digest taken with the built-in hash(), salted per process, instead of SHA-256
clarifying_questions: the same package in two scopes

parts.lesson_anchor: Catalog budget and active context are different budgets (Codex: 2 percent of a known context window; the 8,000-character value only when the size is unknown, never a second cap; descriptions shortened or omitted); Measure the exact serialized catalog sent to the model (Use It 6)
traps: min(2 percent, 8,000) in catalog_budget
a known window also held to 8,000 characters
round instead of rounding down
a window of 0 read as unknown
characters measured against a token budget
the fallback measured in UTF-8 bytes (a Chinese description makes 7,983 characters 8,063 bytes)
cost from name and description lengths instead of the serialized text
shortening from the highest priority, all at once, or after omitting
omitted entries also listed as shortened
input order taken as priority
a catalog at exactly its budget treated as over it (a window whose 2 percent equals the full 2,511-token cost)
parts.integration: the same 33-skill fleet under four budgets: 1,000,000 tokens (everything, 8,415 characters), unknown (5 shortened), 120,000 tokens (7 shortened), 40,000 tokens (12 kept and shortened, 21 omitted)

parts.lesson_anchor: Three disclosure levels (Level 2 body on activation, Level 3 resources read on demand); Branch-specific references beat topic dumps (only declared branches); Loading must be observable (skill.resource.loaded with skill, resource, reason and bytes, no secrets); Exercise 3 (byte limit: exactly at the limit and one byte above)
parts.wire_format: logfmt: one line per request ending in a newline, key=value pairs one space apart in a fixed order, values bare or double-quoted with \\, \", \n, \r, \t and \u00XX escapes, decided by the test's strict parser; events skill.activated, skill.refused, skill.resource.loaded, skill.resource.refused
traps: values with spaces, =, quotes, backslashes or newlines, or empty values, left unquoted or unescaped
a read before activation, or for another skill that is not active
any file in the package readable instead of the declared branches
the declared branch that is a symlink leaving the package (validate_reference from Part 1)
the limit counted in characters (1,000 characters, 1,088 bytes), a file of exactly 1,024 bytes refused
activation bytes counted in characters or over the whole SKILL.md
every request read before the first event (probe: at most one request pulled ahead)
refusal reasons checked out of order: an undeclared traversal path is not_declared, not invalid_path
the stub is an async def without yield: TypeError about __aiter__

parts.lesson_anchor: Branch-specific references beat topic dumps (direct links from SKILL.md, avoid deep chains, keep the graph one hop, 'Read references/ for more' has no load condition); Key Terms: reference graph
traps: links resolved against the package root instead of the linking file's directory, or ./ left in the path
#fragment or ?query kept in the path
depth-first walk keeping the first depth found
links in ``` or ~~~ fenced blocks followed
a directory link expanded into every file under it
non-Markdown files read for links (CHECKS[name](version) in a script)
https: and mailto: links followed as paths
broken links reported by resolved path or with their fragment instead of as written
an existing file outside the package followed instead of reported as broken
dead files searched in the whole package
deep as more than two links instead of two or more
clarifying_questions: an existing file outside the package

deviations: Part 1 defect 3 is a containment check made before resolve() rather than a string-prefix check after it. Chapter 13 already has the prefix-without-a-boundary trap in 12 (URI startswith), 15 (pins picked by prefix without the dot) and 09 (Origin matched by prefix), and a trap class may appear at most twice per chapter. The lesson's own two escapes are covered instead: a symlink to a file outside the package and a symlinked directory, with the host policy allowing in-package symlinks ('decide whether symlinks are allowed; if allowed, check the resolved target every time') and the package reached through a symlinked root. The prefix question is an interviewer follow-up.

Part 1 defect 1 lives in package_dirs, the helper discover_scope shares with the Part 2 cache. A nested example named release-readiness turns the recursion into an equal-rank CollisionError two calls away, on a different call chain.

Part 1 timing uses 1,800 entries instead of 5,000: the quadratic loop at 5,000 entries takes well over 3 seconds. 1,800 keeps the slow version near 2 s with at least 12x on both sides of the 0.15 s limit.

Part 2 does not test atomic replacement. Chapter 13 already tests that trap in 04 and 13, and 15 left it out for the same rule. The reference still writes a temporary file and os.replace, and the interviewer asks about it. Spaces and non-ASCII in paths and newlines in descriptions are in the fixture, but JSON round-trips them, so the traps come from the domain instead: identity by directory, scope policy not cached, JSON types restored, rejections cached, scopes isolated in one snapshot, removed packages and the os.utime mtime reset.

Part 3 counts the 2 percent budget in tokens with an injected count_tokens and the fallback in characters, because the lesson gives the first as a share of the context window and the second as 8,000 characters. The shortening order (lowest priority first, one entry at a time, stop when it fits, then omit lowest priority first) is this host's policy; the lesson only says descriptions may be shortened or omitted. model_json keeps non-ASCII text (ensure_ascii=False), so a Chinese character costs one character; the quiz points out that the lesson's escaped measure inflates such entries six times.

Part 4 gives decision_map (the 'For X, read [file](path).' branches); the candidate writes format_event and the async generator. Besides the lesson's skill.resource.loaded event, activations log the Level 2 body size, refusals carry a reason code and activations of names outside the catalog are refused.
Part 5 adds directory links (reported, not followed), broken links (missing or outside the package), Markdown-only parsing and scheme links to the suggested traps.
Frontmatter parsing is given and untested, to stay clear of lesson 22.
